extracted.intended_audience: federal agency rulewriters, rulemaking officials, and agency counsel
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for agencies on how to engage the public when adopting rules under the APA 'good cause' exemption, including when to use direct final or interim final rulemaking and what procedural disclosures and supplemental engagement to provide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause: 'impracticable' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and comment may be 'impracticable' when an agency 'finds that due and timely execution of its functions would be impeded by the notice otherwise required [by the APA].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply when requiring notice-and-comment would impede timely execution of agency functions. Cite relevant precedent (e.g., Util. Solid Waste Activities Grp. v. EPA). Assess whether delay would materially frustrate statutory or operational deadlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause: 'unnecessary' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and comment may be 'unnecessary' when a rule is 'a routine determination, insignificant in nature and impact, and inconsequential to the industry and to the public' or when the agency lacks discretion regarding the substance of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use only for routine, insignificant, non-discretionary actions. Document why the rule is inconsequential and why public input would not materially inform the outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Good cause: 'contrary to the public interest' standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice and comment may be 'contrary to the public interest' in 'the rare circumstance when ordinary procedures—generally presumed to serve the public interest—would in fact harm that interest.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reserve for exceptional situations where standard notice-and-comment procedures would harm the public interest. Provide a clear factual and legal rationale showing anticipated harm from ordinary procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer direct final rulemaking when 'unnecessary' (except rare non-expeditious cases)
rubrics_metrics.description: Except in the rare instance that an agency determines that direct final rulemaking would not expedite issuance of a rule, an agency should use direct final rulemaking when it: (a) For good cause finds that it is 'unnecessary' to undertake notice-and-comment rulemaking; and (b) Concludes that the rule is unlikely to elicit any significant adverse comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default to direct final when the 'unnecessary' prong applies and the rule is unlikely to be opposed. Agencies should document both the good-cause finding and the assessment that significant adverse comments are unlikely, but may decline direct final if it would not expedite issuance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: identify as 'direct final rule'
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency uses direct final rulemaking, it should publish in the Federal Register a rule that: identifies the rule as a 'direct final rule'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label the Federal Register entry clearly so readers understand the procedure and consequences (e.g., that the rule will take effect only if no significant adverse comments are received).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: explain basis for finding 'unnecessary'
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief statement explaining the basis for the agency’s finding that it is unnecessary to undertake notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the factual and legal basis for invoking the 'unnecessary' prong of good cause so the public and reviewing courts can assess the agency's determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: state basis and purpose and issues considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement of the rule’s basis and purpose and explain the issues the agency considered in developing the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer a succinct explanation of the rule's rationale and the considerations informing its design to aid understanding and enable meaningful comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: provide at least 30-day comment period
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a period of at least 30 days during which interested persons may submit comments regarding the substance of the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 30-day minimum comment window; longer periods may be appropriate depending on complexity. Ensure public notice and clear instructions for submitting comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: explain withdrawal policy if significant adverse comments received
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain that the agency will withdraw the direct final rule if it receives any significant adverse comments and specifies any additional actions that the agency may take if it withdraws the direct final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State the withdrawal procedure and any planned follow-on actions (e.g., proceed with companion proposed rule, reopen notice-and-comment). Clarify timeline and next steps to manage public expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: specify effective date if no significant adverse comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies when the rule will take effect if the agency receives no significant adverse comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an effective date consistent with the Recommendation (see Paragraph 5: generally at least 30 days after close of comment period or after confirmation notice).

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: state whether a confirmation notice will be issued
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicable, specifies whether the agency will issue a subsequent notice in the Federal Register confirming that the agency received no significant adverse comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tell the public whether the agency will publish a confirmation notice; if not publishing one, consider a longer effective date to allow time to withdraw if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: identify any companion proposed rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Identifies any companion proposed rule that will serve as the notice of proposed rulemaking if the agency later withdraws the direct final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using a companion proposed rule, publish it in the same issue if possible and explain that it will become operative if the direct final rule is withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companion proposed rule: provide additional comment period if withdrawn
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency issues a direct final rule, it may consider publishing in the same issue of the Federal Register a companion proposed rule that will serve as a notice of proposed rulemaking if the agency later withdraws the direct final rule. In the event the agency receives significant adverse comments, the agency should consider providing an additional period for public comment on the companion proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawing the direct final rule, allow an additional comment opportunity on the companion proposal to ensure robust public input before finalizing a revised rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'significant adverse comment' in direct final process
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should consider any comment received during direct final rulemaking to be a significant adverse comment if the comment explains why: (a) The rule would be inappropriate, including challenges to the rule’s underlying premise or approach; or (b) The rule would be ineffective or unacceptable without a change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate comments for substantive challenge to premise, approach, or effectiveness. Mere disagreement not grounded in explanation may not suffice; focus on comments that show why the rule is unacceptable as written.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: effective-date timing and confirmation notice guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent exceptional circumstances for providing a different effective date, the agency should provide that a direct final rule will take effect at least 30 days after the close of the comment period if the agency receives no significant adverse comments or at least 30 days after publication of a subsequent notice in the Federal Register confirming that the agency received no significant adverse comments. An agency that does not publish a confirmation notice should consider providing an effective date greater than 30 days after the close of the comment period if the agency believes it is necessary to ensure that it has adequate time to withdraw the rule in the event it receives significant adverse comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 30 days post-comment-period (or post-confirmation) as default. If no confirmation notice will be published, consider a longer lead time to preserve the ability to withdraw the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct final rule: publish withdrawal notice and describe next steps
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency receives any significant adverse comments or otherwise decides to withdraw the direct final rule before it takes effect, the agency should publish a notice in the Federal Register that states that the agency is withdrawing the direct final rule and describes any further rulemaking the agency will conduct on the matter. If the agency previously requested comments in a companion proposed rule as described in Paragraph 3, the agency may proceed with notice-and-comment rulemaking consistent with the proposed rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make withdrawal transparent: state the reasons and explain future rulemaking plans and timelines so stakeholders understand how the issue will proceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage interim final rulemaking when 'impracticable' or 'contrary to the public interest'
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency is encouraged to use interim final rulemaking when it for good cause finds that it is 'impracticable' or 'contrary to the public interest' to undertake notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use interim final when delay would impede functions or when notice-and-comment would harm the public interest. Document the good-cause basis and prepare to solicit and consider post-publication comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: identify as 'interim final rule'
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency uses interim final rulemaking, it should publish in the Federal Register a rule that: identifies the rule as an 'interim final rule'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Label clearly so the public knows the rule is being adopted without prior notice-and-comment but that comments will be solicited and considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: explain basis for finding 'impracticable' or 'contrary to the public interest'
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a brief statement explaining the basis for the agency’s finding that it is 'impracticable' or 'contrary to the public interest' to undertake notice-and-comment rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set out factual/legal justification for invoking the 'impracticable' or 'contrary' prongs, enabling meaningful post-adoption comment and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: state basis and purpose and issues considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement of the rule’s basis and purpose and explains the issues the agency considered in developing the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain rationale and the analytic considerations that led to the interim final rule so commenters can target their input effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: provide appropriate comment period (30 or usually 60 days for major rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides a period of at least 30 days (or in most cases at least 60 days, in particular for 'major rules' as defined in the Congressional Review Act) during which interested persons may submit comments regarding the substance of the rule or the agency’s finding that notice-and-comment rulemaking is impracticable or contrary to the public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Default to 30 days minimum; use 60 days for major rules or where complexity warrants. Allow sufficient time for substantive responses on both rule substance and the agency's good-cause finding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: explain that agency will consider comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that the agency will consider any comments that it receives in response to the interim final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State commitment to consider post-adoption comments and respond in the subsequent final rule; this increases legitimacy and transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: disclose and solicit input on supplemental public engagement plans
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable, sets forth the agency’s plans for supplemental public engagement (see Paragraph 11) and solicits public input on those public engagement plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe planned outreach, listening sessions, RFI's, or other engagement and invite feedback on those plans to improve inclusivity and usefulness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: state effective date and any expiration date
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains that the rule is being adopted without prior notice and comment, specifies the date upon which the rule will take effect, and identifies the rule’s expiration date if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear implementation and expiration timing so regulated parties understand compliance obligations and review cycles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim final rule: state that comments will inform reaffirmation, modification, or withdrawal
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies that the agency will consider the comments and complete the rulemaking by reaffirming, modifying, or withdrawing the interim final rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make explicit that post-publication comments can change the rule and that the agency will issue a subsequent final rule responding to significant comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclude interim final rulemaking with a new final rule responding to significant comments
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should conclude the interim final rulemaking by publishing a new final rule in the Federal Register that responds to all significant comments and reaffirms, modifies, or withdraws the interim final rule as appropriate. Consistent with agency resources and priorities, an agency should publish the new final rule as expeditiously as possible and should prioritize 'major rules' as defined in the Congressional Review Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timely publish a reasoned final rule addressing significant comments. Prioritize resource allocation to ensure major rules receive expedited finalization and responsive treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use additional public engagement before invoking good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: When appropriate, an agency should use additional forms of public engagement, including those identified in Recommendation 2018-7, before considering whether to invoke the good cause exemption when such engagement would help the agency (a) determine if notice-and-comment rulemaking is unnecessary, impracticable, or contrary to the public interest or (b) develop the rule. The agency should explain in the direct or interim final rule what additional public engagement the agency undertook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider RFIs, advance notice, targeted outreach, or listening sessions before invoking good cause to test whether notice-and-comment is truly unavailable or unnecessary; disclose these efforts in the rule document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental engagement after issuing an interim final rule
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency should consider using supplemental forms of public engagement after issuing an interim final rule. Consistent with Executive Order 13,563 and Recommendation 2021-2, an agency should prioritize for retrospective review interim final rules that are 'major rules' as defined in the Congressional Review Act. An agency should explain in any subsequent final rule what supplemental public engagement the agency undertook.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use outreach, listening sessions, RFIs, or post-adoption comment periods to gather information for reconsideration or retrospective review; document these activities in the subsequent final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disclose ex parte communications during supplemental engagement; treat interim final as NPRM equivalent
rubrics_metrics.description: Consistent with Recommendation 2014-4, an agency should disclose ex parte communications that occur during supplemental public engagement. For purposes of applying Recommendation 2014-4, an interim final rule should be considered the equivalent of a notice of proposed rulemaking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply existing ex parte disclosure rules to supplemental engagement around interim final rules; maintain records and publicly disclose ex parte contacts as required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative engagement methods to use when invoking good cause
rubrics_metrics.description: Encourages agencies to use alternative methods—such as publishing requests for information, engaging in targeted outreach, convening listening sessions with interested persons, and soliciting post-adoption comments—to reap the benefits of robust public participation even when they rely properly on the good cause exemption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select among RFIs, targeted outreach, listening sessions, or post-adoption comment periods based on the rule's complexity and affected stakeholders; document the methods used and how they informed the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid needless or counterproductive public engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: The same factors that make a comment period inappropriate may weigh equally against other types of public engagement as well. Neither the agency nor the public is well served by needless or counterproductive efforts to engage the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not undertake public engagement where it would be pointless or harmful. Assess whether engagement would be productive before committing resources; document reasons for forgoing engagement when appropriate.
